upload.title: Why Walmart Opened Stores Right Next to Each Other #shorts
upload.description:
Economist Thomas Holmes mapped every Walmart opening from 1962 to 2005. The stores spread like a ripple around distribution centers, and he estimated each mile closer to a DC was worth about $3,500 a year per store.

Source: Holmes, T. J. (2011). The Diffusion of Wal-Mart and Economies of Density. Econometrica 79(1), 253-302.

Full documentary on the channel: The Machine Behind Walmart.
